rationale: Objective: minimize the max-rank summed NCCL kernel duration (median of 3 separately profiled runs; original baseline 38.09/38.40 ms) subject to step_ms <= 121.95 ms (1.05x 116.14). How the previous feedback changes this attempt: trial-98426ff10f(-param-7e7d0495) selected the two c10d::allreduce_ functional sites, was bitwise exact (max_abs_error 0.0 over 248,879,617 elements), fully covered (12+1), and its rendezvous measurably worked (rank-0 communication median 38.09 -> 36.59), yet failed only step_ms (214.67 > 121.95). The binding_cost AB/BA collector on this exact parent revision (observations/previous-after/binding_cost-2087a4f7.json) isolates the cause as the binding layer: parent arm median step_ms 115.7/119.3 ms vs binding-only passthrough arm 217.0/226.3 ms, i.e. the legacy functional dispatch mode (TorchDispatchMode around the whole run, ~7,240 dispatcher-visible ops per step) adds ~97-107 ms to ANY functional-site bundle before candidate code runs, and the scoped backend cannot resolve those sites (site_parent is the non-module project.invoke boundary). The repair keeps the validated rendezvous but hosts it on the module boundary group b57f55423ea79f2933a2 = call 03e8e3a0a8a549d528e18317 (gpt2.lm_head, phase microbatch_forward_backward, 4 invocations per step on ranks 0 and 1): per binding-contract.md a module-only bundle installs a direct callable boundary with zero functional sites and ~4 Python invocations per step, so the measured +97-107 ms dispatch failure cannot recur; step_ms is predicted ~flat (115-121 ms) with the 5.8 ms constraint headroom intact. Mechanism: parent-exact passthrough of the module forward (original args/kwargs, parent output returned unchanged - identical kernels, autograd graph, gradients and DDP state; the inner aten.view/t/mm/_unsafe_view calls still execute inside the parent call and are neither replaced nor eliminated; the two c10d::allreduce_ sites are not enclosed by this boundary and stay on the parent) followed by one gloo barrier on the adapter's existing state['control'] group (created in prepare, backend gloo, timeout 120 s, already used by before_run outside timing), executed on every invocation: 4 symmetric rendezvous per step, one right after each microbatch's vocabulary projection, before loss/backward. Measured justification (current-revision collectors): the DDP bucket-allreduce CPU submissions show a stable 5.2-6.4 ms cross-rank spread (execution_timeline-1221e205 cross_rank bounds 5.23-6.42 ms at the first collective, decaying only to 5.23-5.50 ms at the last), which the leader's first NCCL kernel absorbs as spin-wait (8114 us ~= 6.2 ms wait + 1.93 ms transfer; nsys-9ed9145c leader extreme 205.7 ms first kernel, remaining 12 kernels at floor), per-microbatch grad_ready lag grows 2.98 -> 5.35 ms across the step (skew is created before the reduction phase), and the per-step transfer floor at the exact observed sizes is ~34.5-35.1 ms (collective_calibration-1af5837f: 1.993 ms x 12 x 28,351,488 B plus 10.61-10.65 ms x 157,541,376 B; LL=SIMPLE within noise, SHM/PCIe transport-bound pair, peer_access 0). Aligning the ranks before each backward caps the lead at about one microbatch, so the leader's first bucket kernel should fall from ~8.1 ms toward the ~2.0 ms transfer time and the residual ~0.5-0.75 ms per-bucket waits should collapse: predicted objective ~35.1-36.5 ms (~1.6-3.0 ms, 4-8%), bounded below by the measured floor. step_ms should stay ~flat because the laggard that defines the max-rank wall passes each barrier immediately while the leader exchanges host-barrier wait for NCCL kernel wait it no longer pays; four gloo barriers cost ~0.1-0.3 ms host each and launch no NCCL or CUDA kernel, so the communication kernel sum is unaffected by the barrier itself. Correctness is structural: no tensor, collective argument, stream or gradient semantic is touched, outputs and gradients are bitwise identical, so the atol=0/rtol=0 exact replica check, the serial-reference gradient/parameter checks (grad 1e-6/1e-4, parameter 1e-6/1e-4), the finite-loss check and the phase/coverage requirement of 4 module invocations inside every adapter.run invocation (warmup, repeats, continuous_steps=2, the 3 profiled diagnostic runs and the inventory-hook run) are all preserved by calling the parent on each invocation. lm_head is bound at instance level, so the evaluator's separate serial-reference model is untouched, and both ranks execute the identical 4 invocations per invocation so barrier counts are symmetric by construction. Rejected with measured cause: re-selecting any functional site (repeats the +97-107 ms dispatch failure under the frozen legacy backend); NCCL_PROTO/ALGO forcing (trial-3ca928eb87: kernels remained RING_LL and SIMPLE gains nothing at these transport-bound sizes); reducing communicated bytes or precision (exact replica check plus grad tolerance forbid it); changing bucket layout (bucket_cap_mb=25 and gradient_as_bucket_view aliasing are frozen in prepare and unreachable from a module boundary); replacing the NCCL backend (request fixes distributed_backend=nccl, communication required); coalescing the 13 buckets (delays comm past the backward tail and risks step_ms; Work-return semantics make deferral unsafe). Explicit unknowns, stated as hypotheses to test: (a) the profiled skew is sampled at n=3 per rank (waiter excess 2.9-6.8 ms); a low-skew run gains little beyond variance capping; (b) residual drift over loss+backward-to-bucket-0 (~0.3-1 ms) and gloo barrier exit jitter (~0.1-0.5 ms) keep the result above the floor; (c) leadership can flip between runs; the symmetric barrier caps whichever rank leads, but a flip between the final barrier and bucket-0 submission would leave a partial wait on the new leader; (d) blocking the leader's host thread at each barrier must not stall its own pipeline more than the in-kernel wait it replaces - the leader's comm train is expected to shorten by more than the added block, which the measured step_ms and the binding_cost receipt must confirm.

setup_work.build_time: build() only inspects context: it reads state['control'] (the gloo group the adapter already created in prepare), resolves context.references['03e8e3a0a8a549d528e18317'] (the bound parent forward), binds context.get('record_route', no-op), and returns one local callable per rank. No GPU work, no collectives, no warmup ops, no parameter or state mutation, no module.forward wrapper installed by the candidate, no environment or NCCL settings, no CUDA Graph capture, no fixture-dependent precomputation.
setup_work.runtime_added: Per step, inside the timed invocation: 4 parent-exact lm_head forward calls plus 4 gloo dist.barrier(group=state['control']) executions (host-only rendezvous on the existing control group; launches no NCCL or CUDA kernel, allocates no device memory). Route labels are recorded per invocation via context['record_route'] during quality execution only.
setup_work.memory: Setup allocation: 0 bytes; no new CUDA allocations, no retained pools, no graphs, no transformed/packed weights. framework.peak_allocated_bytes, lifecycle peak counters and reserved memory are expected unchanged from the parent; nothing moves into or out of graph pools.
setup_work.state_lifecycle: The replacement is stateless across invocations (no per-step flags or counters), so reset(), continuous_steps=2 execution and the separately profiled diagnostic runs see identical behavior; barriers pair only with the peer rank's barrier of the same invocation.

quality_risks: The every-invocation gloo barrier requires symmetric invocation counts on both ranks. Observed counts are 4 per rank in every adapter.run invocation (warmup, repeats, continuous steps, 3 profiled diagnostic runs, inventory-hook run), and lm_head executes once per microbatch forward on both ranks by construction; any hypothetical framework-side isolated single-rank invocation of this module site would block in the barrier until the control group's 120 s timeout, after which the exception is caught, a runtime-failure route label is recorded, and the call degrades to parent-exact passthrough rather than raising.

Objective benefit depends on the sampled cross-rank skew (profiled n=3 per rank, waiter excess 2.9-6.8 ms); a near-zero-skew measured run gains little beyond variance capping, and the floor (~34.5-35.1 ms) bounds the possible improvement.

Residual submit jitter after the final barrier (loss plus backward-to-bucket-0 host work, ~0.3-1 ms in the profiled regime) and gloo barrier exit jitter (~0.1-0.5 ms) remain inside the first kernel; the transfer floor will not be exactly reached.

Leadership can flip between runs and ranks (baseline rank-1 sample 42.69; nsys rank-1 238.93); the barrier is symmetric and caps whichever rank leads, but a rank-role flip between the final barrier and bucket-0 submission would leave a partial wait on the new leader.

step_ms risk is bounded but nonzero: the laggard that defines the max-rank wall passes each barrier immediately and the leader swaps NCCL kernel wait for host barrier wait, four barriers cost ~0.1-0.3 ms host each against 5.8 ms of constraint headroom, and the module boundary adds only ~4 Python invocations per step (no TorchDispatchMode); nevertheless the measured step_ms and the binding_cost receipt must confirm no unexpected dispatch-mode activation for module-only bundles.

Barrier failures are contained but observable: if state['control'] were unavailable the call is installed as parent-exact passthrough with a setup-failure route label (bitwise outputs preserved, no alignment benefit); a runtime barrier exception likewise degrades to passthrough with a runtime-failure label instead of failing the step.
